title: CHILmesh: a fast 2D mesh library for triangular, quadrilateral, and mixed-element grids

creators.name: Kubatko, Ethan J.
creators.affiliation: Computational Hydrodynamics & Informatics Laboratory, The Ohio State University

description:
CHILmesh is a Python library for two-dimensional triangular, quadrilateral and mixed-element meshes used by hydrodynamic models such as ADCIRC. It reads and writes ADCIRC fort.14 and Gmsh files, peels a mesh into element layers from the boundary inward, smooths nodes with FEM, angle-based and truss smoothers, and reports element quality. The layer method follows the QuADMESH+ thesis (Mattioli, 2017). An optional prebuilt C++ backend runs full initialization 8.6 to 14.7 times faster than pure Python. Install with pip install chilmesh (pip install "chilmesh[cpp]" for the C++ backend); the import name is chilmesh.

This release (1.5.5)

Added

  • chilmesh.registry: a standard-library client for the token-gated Valence mesh registry, with list_meshes, fetch_hash, fetch_mesh_bytes, fetch_mesh and download_mesh. Every download is checked against its SHA-256 hash. Set VALENCE_TOKEN; VALENCE_API_URL is an optional override of the default public API.

Changed

  • The registry client sends User-Agent: chilmesh-registry/1, because Cloudflare blocks the default Python-urllib agent.
  • Four bundled meshes (Block_O.14, structuredMesh1.14, annulus_200pts.fort.14, donut_domain.fort.14) carry header-only boundary fixes and a neutral title line, so their SHA-256 values match the registry copies. Node and element data are unchanged.

Fixed

  • read_from_fort14 raises ValueError on a node id of 0 or above the node count, instead of wrapping to the last vertex (#282).
